llm_response:
Here are a few ways to rewrite the paragraph, depending on the specific style of your target journal. 

**Option 1: Bulleted (Highly Recommended for Medical/Scientific Papers)**
*Using bullet points is the best way to present complex statistical data because it makes the comparisons incredibly easy for the reader to digest.*

> In this study, Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to evaluate the validity of serum endoglin in diagnosing preeclampsia (PE). The analysis demonstrated that serum endoglin effectively discriminates between patient groups at the following cutoffs:
> *   **Mild PE vs. Controls:** Cutoff of 5.33; sensitivity 85%, specificity 42.5%, PPV 59.4%, and NPV 73.7% (*p* = 0.076).
> *   **Severe PE vs. Controls:** Cutoff of 5.21; sensitivity 85%, specificity 75%, PPV 77%, and NPV 83% (*p* < 0.001).
> *   **Mild PE vs. Severe PE:** Cutoff of 5.61; sensitivity 90%, specificity 65%, PPV 72%, and NPV 87% (*p* < 0.001).
> 
> These findings are consistent with previous literature. Baumann et al. [24] reported similar results, noting sensitivities and specificities of 63% and 57% for sEng, respectively, and 64% and 56% for sFlt1; combining sEng and inhibin A increased the sensitivity to 68% and the specificity to 61%. Furthermore, our results align with Gaber et al. [10], who demonstrated that serum endoglin achieved a sensitivity of 94.4%, a specificity of 87.5%, and an accuracy of 89.5%.

**Option 2: Paragraph Format (Best for Traditional Article formatting)**
*If you are restricted to standard paragraph text, this version breaks the long run-on sentence into distinct, readable parts.*

> In this study, Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to evaluate the diagnostic validity of serum endoglin for preeclampsia (PE). When distinguishing between mild PE and controls, serum endoglin had a cutoff of 5.33, yielding a sensitivity of 85%, specificity of 42.5%, positive predictive value (PPV) of 59.4%, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 73.7% (*p* = 0.076). To discriminate between severe PE and controls, the cutoff was 5.21, resulting in a sensitivity of 85%, specificity of 75%, PPV of 77%, and NPV of 83% (*p* < 0.001). Furthermore, the biomarker distinguished mild PE from severe PE at a cutoff of 5.61, with a sensitivity of 90%, specificity of 65%, PPV of 72%, and NPV of 87% (*p* < 0.001). Our results are consistent with previous research; for example, Baumann et al. [24] reported sensitivities and specificities for predicting PE of 63% and 57% for sEng and 64% and 56% for sFlt1. When sEng and inhibin A were combined, their sensitivity increased to 68% with a specificity of 61%. Similarly, our findings align with Gaber et al. [10], who demonstrated that serum endoglin achieved a sensitivity of 94.4%, a specificity of 87.5%, and an overall accuracy of 89.5%.

**Key Improvements Made:**
*   **Grammar & Phrasing:** Removed awkward phrasing like "In this study as regard to the use of..." and replaced it with standard academic phrasing. 
*   **Punctuation & Spacing:** Fixed missing spaces (e.g., "sensitivity90", "Baumannet"), corrected hyphens, and changed "p value" to the standard academic format (*p*).
*   **Flow:** Grouped the comparisons logically (Study findings -> Comparison to Baumann -> Comparison to Gaber) and varied the sentence structure so it doesn't sound repetitive. 
*   **Data Preservation:** Double-checked that every single statistic, cutoff, reference, and variable name remains exactly as you provided it.
